item.title: Four More Pages: historical fiction, comic books with Jack Kessler
item.description: On this episode of Four More Pages, Mya is joined by Weekend Anchor and Reporter Jack Kessler.

item.title: Vance visits Austin for fundraiser with $50,000 cover charge
item.description: Vice President J.D. Vance is traveling to Austin to attend a fundraising event hosted by Palantir co-founder Joe Lonsdale, where donors must pledge $50,000 or more, while Texas State Rep. Christina Morales criticizes Vance for focusing on wealthy tech billionaires instead of working families.

item.title: 2026 Remarkable Women: Kara Gaut
item.description: She turned compassion into a calling and built an organization that’s changing lives across the Panhandle. Kara Gaut, founder and CEO of Children’s Home Healthcare, is being recognized as a 2026 local Remarkable Women finalist for her dedication to caring for children and supporting families when they need it most.

item.title: Red Cross Giving Day encourages support for families affected by disasters
item.description: Red Cross Giving Day is Wednesday, and the American Red Cross North Texas Region is encouraging the community to come together to support families impacted by disasters and emergencies.

item.title: Amarillo folk-rock band Plemons Bridge to perform on KWTS' Live Lounge series
item.description: A folk-rock band from Amarillo will perform next in the West Texas A&amp;M University concert series, showcasing their rising popularity in the local music scene.

item.title: March to April Weather
item.description: Hello everyone, and welcome to April! This afternoon will continue mostly cloudy, humid, and seasonal with high temperatures in the cool 60's and 70's. Amarillo should top out close to 75. Also, hit or miss April showers and embedded thunderstorms are possible for the rest of today and tonight. Any severe weather should be limited [...]

item.title: Amarillo ISD announces flexible learning option
item.description: Beginning in August 2026 Amarillo Independent School District is set to introduce Amarillo ISD Online for students in grades 6-12.

item.title: DPS troopers seize drugs in Carson County traffic stop
item.description: The Texas Department of Public Safety reported that troopers seized multiple drugs in a traffic stop on March 26.

item.title: Texas Historical Commission hosting events celebrating Texas history
item.description: The Texas Historical Commission is celebrating the 250th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence with some events celebrating Texas history.

item.title: Braden Hausen, AHS alumni, reflects on historic March Madness run
item.description: For Amarillo High alumn and native Braden Hausen, March Madness wasn’t just about basketball; it was about history, family, and proving where hard work can take you.

item.title: Amarillo Police investigate firearm incident that put 2 schools into lockdown Wednesday
item.description: AMARILLO, Texas (KAMR/KCIT) — The Amarillo Police Department reported that two schools were placed in secure status as a precaution after a man discharged a firearm in a backyard. item.title: Texas will fully fund clinical trials into the medical effects of ibogaine
item.description: A program designed to conduct drug development clinical trials for a psychedelic drug in Texas hit a road bump after the state could not find a drug company to help develop a FDA-approved drug.

item.title: Legal challenges filed over proposed horse racing license relocation to Clovis
item.description: Multiple groups have filed legal challenges against a decision to relocate a horse license from Farmington to Clovis, according to court documents.

item.title: Dumas PD reports death of retired K-9 unit 'Ronin'
item.description: The Dumas Police Department reported that one of its retired K-9 units "Ronin" has died from health-related complications.
